advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard `gc_schema_for` against a version string with no dot so `minor` defaults to 0 rather than duplicating the major.
evidence: ABSENCE: no test exercises a dotless BuildKit version string through gc_schema_for; parametrized versions all contain a minor component
advisory.finding: `gc_schema_for` derives `minor` via `rest="${1#*.}"` which, for a version string containing no dot (e.g. a bare major like `"1"` or a probe that returned only digits), leaves `rest` equal to the whole string and thus `minor` equal to the major rather than 0. For DOCKER_MODERN_GC_BUILDKIT_MAJOR=0 this is masked because any major>0 short-circuits to modern and a bare `"0"` would set minor='0'; but the parsing is incorrect in the general case and would misclassify if the boundary major were ever nonzero.
advisory.suggested_fix: After extracting rest, add: `case "$1" in *.*) : ;; *) rest=0 ;; esac` before computing minor.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture and check the `docker buildx inspect` exit status (or require a full GC-policy block) before trusting parsed keep-bytes/version, so a failed-but-nonempty inspect degrades to UNVERIFIED rather than a spurious verdict.
evidence: ABSENCE: neither call captures or checks `docker buildx inspect` returncode; a non-zero exit with partial stdout is indistinguishable from a clean read
advisory.finding: `report_effective_gc_policy` and `probe_buildkit_version` both parse `docker buildx inspect` with stderr discarded and never inspect the command's exit status. A buildx that fails partway (non-zero exit) but has already emitted a matching `Keep Bytes:`/`Buildkit:` line to stdout is treated as authoritative; the guard is only the empty-capture check, so a truncated/garbled-but-parseable line can produce a false MATCH or a wrong version verdict rather than UNVERIFIED.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the readback cannot report enforcement from a filtered sub-policy alone (e.g. require the catch-all/unfiltered rule to be present), so a partial inspect block cannot yield a false MATCH.
evidence: 234:  sys.exit(0 if abs(sizes[widest] - cap) <= cap * tolerance else 1)
ABSENCE: no check that the matched rule is the unfiltered catch-all; the 'largest' heuristic assumes the catch-all is always emitted and always numerically largest
advisory.finding: The effective-policy readback compares against the LARGEST reported Keep Bytes to avoid mistaking the narrow filtered rule for the cap, but there is no assertion that a catch-all/unfiltered rule was actually present. If `docker buildx inspect` reports ONLY the filtered sub-policy rule(s) (e.g. a BuildKit version that emits a reduced policy block), the largest of those sub-policy numbers is compared to the cap and could coincidentally fall within 1% and be reported as 'IS being enforced' when the true ceiling was never observed.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wrap the `docker buildx inspect` calls in `probe_buildkit_version` and `report_effective_gc_policy` in an explicit `timeout` so the documented 'bounded / never hang a boot orchestrator' guarantee is actually enforced.
evidence: infra/scripts/docker-storage-cap.sh:270 comment: "Bounded: a wedged daemon must not hang a boot orchestrator."
`search_files timeout` over infra/scripts/docker-storage-cap.sh returned `(no matches)` — no timeout guard backs the boundedness claim
advisory.finding: The BuildKit version probe and effective-policy read-back are documented as 'Bounded' against a wedged daemon hanging a boot orchestrator, but neither `docker buildx inspect` call is wrapped in a `timeout`; there is no timeout anywhere in the script, so a hung daemon can block --install indefinitely on the boot path.
scenarios: A dockerd that is up but wedged (deadlocked builder / stuck default builder init) causes `docker buildx inspect` to block; --install (invoked at boot per the orchestrator) hangs instead of degrading to the loud-log fallback the comments promise.
advisory.suggested_fix: Prefix both `docker buildx inspect` invocations with `timeout <N>s` (e.g. `timeout 10s docker buildx inspect`) and treat a non-zero timeout exit as the existing 'unreadable' branch (render modern schema / report UNVERIFIED).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a readback test with a present-but-uninterpretable keep-bytes value (e.g. '5PiB' or 'unlimited') asserting UNVERIFIED and that 'IS being enforced' is absent.
evidence: infra/scripts/docker-storage-cap.sh:226 `if not sizes or any(size is None for size in sizes):` -> `raise SystemExit(2)`
test_an_unreadable_effective_policy_is_reported_as_unverified uses `buildkit_keep_bytes=""`, which hits the `[ -z "$reported" ]` branch at line 196, NOT the SystemExit(2)/status==2 branch
The docker stub in _bindir only ever emits well-formed sizes or nothing; no test injects a keep-bytes value like '5PiB' or 'unlimited' that as_bytes returns None for
advisory.finding: The parse-failure UNVERIFIED branch of report_effective_gc_policy (embedded Python raising SystemExit(2) when a `Keep Bytes:` value is present but uninterpretable, handled at shell lines 238-241) is never exercised. Every readback test supplies either a well-formed size (5GiB / 5.588GiB / 790.6MiB) or an empty buildkit_keep_bytes, so the only UNVERIFIED path covered is the distinct empty-`reported` branch at line 196. A value BuildKit could print that as_bytes rejects — e.g. an unit not in UNITS ('5PiB') or a non-numeric token ('unlimited') — would exercise the uninterpretable path, whose regression would be silently uncaught.
scenarios: BuildKit reports a keep-bytes value in a unit or format the parser does not recognise; the script should report UNVERIFIED but a regression collapsing that branch (e.g. treating a parse failure as agreement) would go undetected
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test parameterising buildkit_keep_bytes to a value as_bytes rejects (unknown unit or non-numeric), asserting `"UNVERIFIED" in result.stderr` and `"IS being enforced" not in result.stderr`.
